name: the Earth and the Moon
plain: The Earth at its mean radius (6371 km) with day and night from the Sun's place now (the Astronomical Almanac's low-precision formula, good to 0.01 degrees); the Moon at its mean radius (1737 km) and mean distance (384,400 km) on an orbit tilted 5.1 degrees, placed to about 0.3 degrees and never drawn under 3 pixels, its night side at three tenths of full light so that it can be found; a ring marks the Earth once it is a speck. No land, cloud or ice is drawn.

carrier.state: the Earth and the Moon at their mean radii and distance, placed for the host's clock

source.external: The Astronomical Almanac, low-precision formula for the Sun's position (good to 0.01 degrees)
Mean radii of the Earth (6371 km) and the Moon (1737 km), the Moon's mean distance (384,400 km) and orbital tilt (5.1 degrees): rounded textbook values; no catalogue is named in the code

views.reads: the rung's marks at the zoom's metres per pixel

budget.quantity: what drawing a tile coarse may move against drawing it fine: the draw allocator's tolerance (Acuity, eps_px). It is not a bound on the picture's faithfulness to the holon.

draw.label: catalogue values
draw.fade_owed: The ground rung is of no particular place and the Earth rung is the Earth. They meet only when no host draws the band between them; with a host (the CEWP twin) the host's globe stands there, and its sun replaces the almanac's. Only the unhosted ladder is declared and checked.
